model_annotation: This line plot illustrates how coverage changes as the number of completions (k) increases for three different models: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k)”, uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2^0 to 2^8, with tick marks at intervals of 2^i where i increments by one. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage”, is linear and ranges from 0.0 to 0.8. The plot displays three distinct lines: the Llama-3B model is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; the Llama-3B + FT model is shown as a dashed green line with square markers; and the Llama-1B + FT model is depicted as a dashed light blue line with diamond markers. All three lines start at low coverage values (approximately 0.4 for Llama-3B, 0.2 for Llama-3B + FT, and 0.1 for Llama-1B + FT at k=2^0) and exhibit an upward trend, peaking near k=2^6 or k=2^7, before gradually declining toward the end of the range. The Llama-3B line consistently remains above the other two throughout the entire range of k values shown.
